options.A: A query in one modality retrieves relevant evidence in another modality.
options.B: A text query retrieves only text passages using two identical indexes.
options.C: A generator produces longer answers without retrieving evidence.
options.D: A system ranks documents only by their file size.

questions.explanation: Cross-modal retrieval connects query and evidence across modalities, such as text-to-image or image-to-text, using compatible representations or mappings.

questions.text: Text and image retrievers return scores on very different numeric scales. What should you address before interpreting their weighted sum as balanced evidence?

options.A: Make all retrieved items have identical filenames.
options.B: Discard all source identities so the generator sees only scores.
options.C: Normalize or calibrate scores and evaluate the fusion weights on the task.
options.D: Assume the retriever with larger raw numbers is more reliable.

questions.explanation: Uncalibrated score scales can dominate fusion regardless of evidence quality. Normalization or calibration and task evaluation make the weighting meaningful.

questions.text: The toy sets confidence=top[0][1], where the value is a weighted retrieval score, then compares it with confidence_floor. What does this confidence actually represent?

options.A: A calibrated probability that every answer claim is correct.
options.B: The top fused retrieval score used as a heuristic threshold.
options.C: A verified measure of agreement between independent human graders.
options.D: The fraction of generated claims proven by their cited sources.

questions.explanation: The code reuses the fused ranking score as confidence. It does not calibrate a probability or verify answer claims.
